info.title: Ahoy control plane API
info.summary: UI-independent HTTP/JSON contract for hosted Ahoy story deliveries.
info.description:
The public boundary for any Ahoy client (Angular UI, CLI, scripts). Clients never
call the SDK worker, read run directories or see Copilot tokens.

Conventions:
- Every mutation records the authenticated actor and is rejected when stale
  (`expectedVersion` does not match the story's `version`) or a duplicate
  (for example a second decision at the same gate). Nothing is silently advanced.
- Commands that the reconciler completes asynchronously return `202` with the
  updated story; watch `/events/stream` or poll the read endpoints for the outcome.
- Costs are integers in nano-AIU (1 AIU = 1_000_000_000 nano-AIU).
- Errors use RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code`.
  Requests are validated against this document: unknown or repeated query parameters and
  invalid path, query, header or body values answer `400 validation_failed` with `errors`, as does body
  text Postgres cannot store (a NUL character or an unpaired surrogate);
  a method the path does not support answers `400 bad_request` with an `Allow` header. Any
  operation may answer `500 internal_error`.
- Incompatible changes require a new major version (`/api/v2`).
- A story's state lives in Postgres (`getStoryState`); artifacts are the files its agents wrote. A story created
  before the relational state model (migration 0002) can still be read, but every change, its state and any
  artifact whose bytes are not in Postgres answer `409 legacy_story`.

Every request except `/health` must carry a WebEAM (ForgeRock AM, Alpha realm) access token in
`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`. The API introspects the token at WebEAM (RFC 7662) with its client ID and
secret; the token's `sub` is the acting user. A missing or invalid
token answers `401 unauthenticated`. The `X-Ahoy-Actor` header is accepted only when the
server runs with `AHOY_AUTH=dev` (local POC).

200.description: The API and database are reachable.

get.summary: The models a person may choose for a story's phases, and what each phase runs on by default.
get.description:
The catalogue is configured on the server, not read from a Copilot account: `AHOY_MODEL_CATALOG` (a JSON
file, `source: file`) or the built-in list (`source: built_in`). Every model the server's phase
configuration names is listed too, so a default is always one a person can pick. `reasoningEfforts` of a
model is null when the catalogue does not say which efforts it takes; `[]` means it takes none.

Choosing a model outside this list is still accepted by `startStory` and `setStoryModels`: whether the owner's
Copilot account may use a model, and whether it takes the effort, is checked by the worker before it sends a
prompt (0 AIU); a run refused there fails and the story halts.

`defaults` is what each slot of a story started now (without `controlRef`) runs on when nobody chooses: the
server's phase configuration, then `phases.tsv` at the control repo's HEAD (`controlSha`). When the control
repo cannot be read, `controlSha` is null and the defaults come from the configuration alone.

get.summary: All Jira Stories, Tasks and Bugs matching the configured backlog query.
get.description:
Read-only Jira Server REST search, authenticated with the server's `JIRA_PAT`, not the client's
WebEAM token. Requires `JIRA_BASE_URL` (HTTPS) and `JIRA_PAT` on the API process; neither is returned.
`JIRA_BACKLOG_JQL` overrides the server-side query. When unset, the default JQL is:
`project = R3DA AND issuetype in (Story, Task, Bug) AND status in (New, "In Specification", Open, "In Test")
AND "Feature Team" = aaa AND Team in (34115) ORDER BY Rank ASC`.

The default is the workspace's start-page availability filter with Stories, Tasks and Bugs, not the Jira Agile
board backlog (which excludes sprint-assigned issues). The query must select only Story, Task and Bug
issues; other issue types cause `503 unavailable`. Epics are not supported. No query parameters
are accepted. The backend follows all Jira search pages and preserves rank order; `total` equals
the number of returned items. Issues already started in Ahoy are not excluded.

A successful result is cached on the server for 30 seconds. No stale or partial result is served.
Missing configuration, Jira HTTP errors (including PAT rejection or rate limiting), network/timeout
errors, malformed responses or pagination inconsistencies return `503 unavailable`.
This lookup never starts a delivery or spends AIU.

200.description: Complete backlog in Jira rank order.

post.summary: Start a story at intake. The actor becomes its owner and runs bill the owner's token.
post.description:
`models` may choose the model and reasoning effort of each phase from the start (`intake`, `planning`,
`implementation` and `review`, the one reviewer of `pr_review`); what is left out runs on the server's phase
configuration, then the pinned `phases.tsv`, then the agent's own profile. `GET /stories/{key}/models` shows
what each phase will get. A `models` that names an unknown slot, an empty choice, a model or effort no run can
take, or `null` answers `400 validation_failed`, and no story is created.

201.description: The story was created in phase `intake`; the reconciler will dispatch Navigator.

post.summary: Halt the story and cancel its active run, if any. The phase does not change.

202.description: The story is halted; cancellation of an active run completes asynchronously.

post.summary: Clear a halt so the reconciler retries the current phase. May spend AIU.

202.description: The story is ready to be stepped again.

post.summary: Change the story's total AIU cap. May allow further spend.
post.description:
Takes effect when the reconciler next queues a run; an active run keeps the cap it started with.
The new cap must not be below what the story has already spent. Status and phase do not change,
so a halted story still needs `resume`.

202.description: The story with its new budget.

get.summary: The model and reasoning effort each phase of the story runs on, and where each comes from.
get.description:
One entry per slot of the story's model plan: `intake`, `planning`, `implementation`, and `review` (the one
reviewer of `pr_review`). `chosen` is what a person chose for the story;
`model` and `reasoningEffort` are what the slot's next run gets once the server's phase configuration and the
pinned `phases.tsv` fill in what was not chosen. A choice applies as a pair: an effort configured for another
model is not carried onto a model a person chose, which then runs at its own default effort. Whether the
owner's Copilot account may use the model, and whether the model takes the effort, is checked by the worker
before it sends a prompt (0 AIU); a run refused there fails and the story halts.

post.summary: Choose the model and reasoning effort for some phases of the story.

202.description: The story's model plan after the change, at the story's new version.

200.description: Every question asked for the story, in order.

post.summary: Record one human answer. Answers are never replaced; the next run consumes them.

202.description:
The answer is recorded. When it was the last pending question the story becomes
`ready` and the reconciler starts a new run of the same phase.

get.summary: Automated gate verdicts and human decisions, oldest first.

post.summary: Approve, send back or reject at a human gate. Silence is never approval.

202.description: The decision is recorded and the story is routed per the phase table.

post.summary: Settle a review the review gate halted on, by sending the work to rework or overriding the review.
post.description:
Only for a story halted on the review gate (`gate_halt` or `gate_rejected`) in a review phase. `rework`
charges the rework ceiling and reopens the work the findings name, or exactly `packages`. `override` moves the
story to the delivery gate, which still needs a person's decision. Reworking may spend AIU.

202.description: The decision is applied; the story is ready (or terminal at `blocked`).

post.summary: Retry or accept a work package nothing else will move (failed, stalled, blocked or unverified).
post.description:
Only while the story is halted in implementation. `retry` sends the package round again with `reason` as its
rework note (may spend AIU); `accept` marks it done as it stands. The repository is still checked by
`child_ready` before review.

202.description: The decision is applied and the story is ready.

post.summary: Send delivered work packages round again by hand, from a halted implementation or review.
post.description:
Reopens `packages` (even in a merged repository), or the delivered packages of `repos`, or all delivered
packages, with `note` as their rework note, and moves the story to implementation. No rework round is charged.
May spend AIU. A delivery gate is sent back with a decision instead.

202.description: The packages are reopened and the story is ready.

post.summary: Take a story out of `blocked`, back to the phase it was blocked from, with more rework rounds.
post.description:
Raises the rework ceiling of each repository at it (or of each of `repos`) by `rounds`, then returns the story
to the phase that moved it to `blocked`, which evaluates its gate again. A story blocked by a person's
rejection at a human gate cannot be unblocked. May spend AIU.

get.summary: The story's state, as a worker's `state.json` shows it to the agents.
get.description: Rendered from the story's typed tables in Postgres, where the state lives: acceptance criteria, work packages, child repositories, reviews, human gates, revisions, the gate rejection, `gate_results` (from the gate records) and `decision_log` (from the `decisions` table). The field names follow the control repo's `state.json`; fields the agents wrote that no rule reads are passed through as they wrote them. A reviewer's report shows the fields the review gate reads; the report as written is in its `review.reported` event.

get.summary: The story's current artifact set (Jira snapshot, plan and the other files its agents wrote).

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Artifact-set revision; defaults to the current one.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: An ETag from an earlier response; a match answers 304 without a body.

ETag.description: The quoted sha256 of the content.

304.description: The content has not changed since the given ETag.

get.description:
Each message is `id: <Event.id>`, `event: <Event.type>` and one `data:` line holding the
`Event` JSON. IDs are stable and increase monotonically. To resume, reconnect with the
`Last-Event-ID` header (or `after`); the server replays every later event before streaming
new ones. Comment lines (`: keepalive`) are sent periodically. Clients that cannot use SSE
may poll `listStoryEvents` instead.

webeam.description: WebEAM (Alpha realm) access token. The `sub` claim is the acting user.

devActor.name: X-Ahoy-Actor
devActor.description: Local POC only; honoured when the server runs with AHOY_AUTH=dev. The value is the acting user's ID.

After.name: after
After.description: Return only events with a greater ID.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 problem details.

Version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; increases on every story change.

Phase.description: A phase from the pinned control repo's `phases.tsv`.

StoryStatus.description:
`ready`: the reconciler will act. `running`: a worker run is active.
`awaiting_input`: questions need answers. `awaiting_decision`: a human gate is open.
`halted`: stopped for `haltReason` until a person resumes it. `terminal`: done or blocked.

sprint.description:
Selected from Jira customfield_10000: active first, then future, then closed; the lowest
sprint ID breaks ties. Null when unassigned. Supports Jira Server's legacy sprint strings.

controlSha.description: Control-repo commit (agents, skills, phase rules) pinned for the story's life.

budgetNanoAiu.description: Hard AIU cap for every run of the story together.

controlRef.description: Control-repo commit to pin. Defaults to the configured control repo's HEAD.

models.description: The model and reasoning effort for each phase; a slot left out runs on the server's configured defaults. Can be changed later with `setStoryModels`.

WorkPackageId.description: A work package id from the plan, e.g. `WP1`.

RepoAlias.description: A plan alias of a child repository, as in `child_repos[].repo`.

packages.description: `rework` only: reopen exactly these packages instead of the ones the findings name.

note.description: The rework note the implementer gets.

budgetNanoAiu.description: New hard AIU cap for every run of the story together, including what is already spent.

ModelSlot.description: A part of the story that runs on one model, by phase; `review` is the one reviewer of `pr_review`.

ModelId.description: A Copilot model id, e.g. `claude-sonnet-5` or `gpt-5.6-terra`.

ReasoningEffort.description: The Copilot SDK's reasoning effort levels; a model may accept fewer, or none.

ModelChoice.description: A model, a reasoning effort, or both; what is left out comes from the defaults.

ModelPlanChange.description: A choice per slot to change; `null` gives a slot back to the configured defaults.

chosen.description: What a person chose for the story; null when the slot runs on the defaults.

model.description: The model the slot's next run gets; null leaves it to the agent profile.

reasoningEffort.description: The effort the slot's next run gets; null is the model's own default.

modelSource.description: `revision`: a one-round override for the phase the story is in; `story`: the person's choice; `configuration`: the server's phase configuration; `phase_table`: the pinned `phases.tsv`; `agent_profile`: no model is named, so the agent's own profile decides.

label.description: What a person reads; the id when none is configured.

reasoningEfforts.description: The efforts the model takes (`[]`, none); null when the catalogue does not say.

SlotDefault.description: What a slot of a story started now runs on when nobody chooses (a `SlotModel` without `chosen`).

model.description: The model; null leaves it to the agent profile.

reasoningEffort.description: The effort; null is the model's own default.

source.description: Where the list came from; neither is checked against a Copilot account.

reasoningEfforts.description: Every effort `startStory` and `setStoryModels` accept; a model may take fewer.

controlSha.description: The control commit whose `phases.tsv` filled the defaults; null when it could not be read.

model.description: The model the run was started with; null leaves it to the agent profile.

reasoningEffort.description: The reasoning effort the run was started with; null is the model's own default.

runtime.description: Where the worker ran, e.g. `docker`, `k8s` (one Kubernetes Job), `replay` (offline re-use of recorded evidence) or `fake`.

replayOf.description: For runtime `replay`, the recorded worker run whose outputs were re-used. Its usage is not charged again, so `usage` is zero.

gate.description: The verdict of the gate that judged this run's output, from the story's gate records.

source.description: `gate`: an automated gate the harness ran. `human`: a recorded decision.

gate.description: Gate name (`intake`, `plan`) or human gate key (`plan_accepted`).
Human gate key from the phase table, e.g. `plan_accepted`.

decision.description:
`approve` advances per the phase table. `send_back` returns the story to the phase
that produced the artifact with `reason` for the agent (counts a revision round).
`reject` moves the story to `blocked`. `send_back` and `reject` require `reason`.

revision.description: The artifact-set revision this entry belongs to (every revision is a complete set).

EventType.description: Stable event type. New types may be added in a minor version; clients must ignore unknown types.

payload.description: Type-specific JSON; never contains tokens or credentials. A `run.progress` payload is a `RunProgressPayload`. A `run.waiting` event says the story's next run is waiting for a run slot: the server allows at most `maxActiveRuns` runs queued or running at once (`AHOY_MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS`, one worker container or pod each), and `activeRuns` were when the story looked. Its payload is `{phase, activeRuns, maxActiveRuns}`. It is written once when the wait starts; the story stays `ready` at the same version and its run is queued (`run.queued`) when a slot frees.

RunProgressPayload.description:
The payload of a `run.progress` event: what a running agent is doing. The worker writes each step of its
session to the run's `events.jsonl` as it goes; while the run is running the reconciler reads the new lines
on each poll (about every 2 seconds, `AHOY_POLL_MS`, at most 4 MiB a poll) and once more when the run ends,
then to the end of the log (up to 64 MiB), so the run's last steps come before its `run.finished`. Each poll
that found steps writes them, then one `spend` event:

- `tool`: a tool call the agent started: the tool's name and a short summary of its main argument (a path,
  a pattern, a query, a URL, a command, a description or an intent), when it has one;
- `message`: the first 200 characters of a message the agent wrote, on one line;
- `spend`: the run's spend so far (summed from the log the same way the worker sums it) and counts. It closes
  every batch, so it also says where the reconciler stopped reading (`line`, `offset`); a restarted
  reconciler goes on from there and never writes a step twice. A poll that found only spend or counts writes
  one at most every 30 seconds, and always on the poll that sees the run end.

Texts are plain (no control characters or terminal escapes, whitespace collapsed) and credential-shaped
strings are masked as `[REDACTED]`, as in a halt's `workerLog`. Limits: at most 10 steps per poll, the
latest; at most 200 steps per run, after which only `spend` events are written, so the spend and `omitted`
keep moving to the end; at most 1000 events per run, a guard that a run reaches only long after its own
deadline, after which nothing more until `run.finished`. Steps left out are counted in `omitted`, lines that
could not be read (not JSON, or over 1 MiB) in `skipped`. Progress is shown, never judged: a run's outcome and what is
charged come only from `run.finished`, and a run that is cancelled, killed or lost may have shown steps that
no result reflects.

nanoAiu.description: Spent so far by the run, as its log shows it; `run.finished` has what is charged.

steps.description: `tool` and `message` events written for the run.

omitted.description: Steps left out by the limits.

skipped.description: Lines that could not be read.

events.description: `run.progress` events written for the run, this one included.
